item.title: The NFL should relocate the Steelers-Saints game in Paris to London
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: NFL scraps multiple Saturday events due to ongoing protests.
item.content:encoded:
With one day more to go until the Steelers and Saints play in Paris, the NFL shouldn't wait one hour more to relocate the game.

No matter how safe and secure Stade de France will be for the game, it's not safe for NFL fans to be in Paris due to protests that from time to time morph into full-blown riots.

Consider the latest moves made by the league as to the collateral activities. Via the Associated Press, the NFL announced on Saturday the closure of its "NFL House" event, due to "potential accessibility issues." Previously, the Steelers Fan House event was scrapped. The "Saints House" has been postponed until Sunday.

Meanwhile, the U.S. State Department issued a security alert cautioning "Americans in Paris for the NFL game" to "exercise caution and be aware of their surroundings."

Why would the NFL insist on pressing forward? The risk, however big or small it may be, isn't worth it.

The league has said security at the game will be enhanced. Which necessarily means security resources that could be utilized elsewhere in the city are being devoted to something that is far from a necessity.

Also, no matter how secure the stadium is, the fans who have bought tickets to the game will need to get to the perimeter where the NFL's security plan activates.

A soccer match between PSG and Lyon recently was moved from Sunday to Monday, at the direction of French authorities. If the NFL won't do the prudent thing and move the game to London, the powers-that-be in Paris should direct the NFL to bump Steelers-Saints to Monday, too. (That would shift the game broadcast to Monday morning or afternoon, New York time. Which could inadvertently unlock a new standalone window for future NFL games.)

It's surprising that it's gotten to this point. The warning signs have been obvious for weeks. On Friday, even the President chimed in. And the league's determination (or, more accurately, stubbornness) to proceed has led to a situation in which the NFL may still be forced to make an eleventh-hour-and-fifty-seventh-minute decision to do something other than play the game as scheduled. Which, for the teams, will only add to the overall in-season inconvenience of traveling to another country to play a football game.

There's no reason to wait. They should make the move now.

We're not privy to all of the specifics. The generalities continue to suggest that the league absolutely should pivot from the plan to play in Paris at 3:30 p.m. local time on Sunday.

Why assume the risk that any fan will be endangered as they try to get to the game? Why take any risks that the enhanced security will be overrun by an event that the protester-rioters could see as a perfect opportunity to make their message resonate internationally?

It seems to be increasingly obvious that relocation of the game is the right call. Even if nothing happens, there's already a cloud over the league's first-ever Paris game. And if there's even one incident in connection with playing the game as planned, the NFL will risk being dubbed what the French call les incompétents.

item.title: Rhamondre Stevenson says Bears' defensive alignment helped with 48-yard TD
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson made one of the most stunning plays of this NFL season when he turned a short pass at the end of the first half and ran for a 48-yard touchdown against the Bears.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson made one of the most stunning plays of this NFL season when he turned a short pass at the end of the first half and ran for a 48-yard touchdown against the Bears. Stevenson said the Bears' defensive alignment made it possible.

The Bears were so concerned about giving up a Hail Mary on the last play of the half that they put two defensive backs near the goal line, almost 50 yards downfield. The Bears also rushed six to try to prevent Patriots quarterback Drake Maye from having time to set up for a Hail Mary. But that meant the middle of the field was wide open.

"It's kind of how they lined up pre-snap that got us into that play," Stevenson said.

The Bears' defense seemed to be caught off-guard, not expecting Maye to dump it off to Stevenson only a yard past the line of scrimmage. And it's not surprising the Bears weren't expecting it, as scoring a touchdown in that situation is almost unheard of: According to Doug Clawson of CBS Sports, there have been 1,006 plays in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, starting more than 40 yards from the end zone, in which the ball was thrown less than 10 yards downfield, and Stevenson's catch was the only one of those 1,006 plays that turned into a touchdown.

"I was just trying to make a play, put my team in a position to swing the game a little bit, as much as we can," Stevenson said. "We've been working on that play for a long time and it came in handy today. Executed on that play so it felt good to do that."

Asked what his mindset was when Maye threw him the Ball, Stevenson answered, "Score."

He did that, producing one of the best touchdowns of this NFL season.

item.title: Bears lead NFL in time of possession, but Ben Johnson would prefer one-play TD drives
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: ""I've never been one for the time of possession stat. I don't know that that really equates to winning and losing," Johnson said.
item.content:encoded:
The Bears lead the NFL in time of possession, but that doesn't matter to coach Ben Johnson.

"I've never been one for the time of possession stat. I don't know that that really equates to winning and losing, necessarily. And yet when you look up, we were possessing the ball more than our opponent more often than not," Johnson said.

The Bears' average time of possession of 35:30 per 60-minute game is the highest in the NFL, they've run 505 offensive plays this season, which is by far the most of any team, and they're the only team averaging more than 70 offensive plays per game. Johnson said he thinks about how long drives affect players, both on offense and defense, but that he's ultimately happier when his offense scores quickly than slowly.

"It's not something that we stress," Johnson said. "We really talk more about getting explosive plays. I would rather have a one-play drive for a touchdown than a 10-play drive for a touchdown. But the ability to stay efficient, stay on schedule, I think that's something that good offenses show that they can do."

The Bears have shown they're a good offense, even if sometimes it takes them longer to get into the end zone than Johnson would like.

item.title: Lions' Sam LaPorta clarifies contract comments: "I want to play for this team"
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Lions' tight end is hoping to get a contract extension from the Lions.
item.content:encoded:
Lions tight end Sam LaPorta said this week that if he doesn't get a new contract from the Lions, he’ll go get paid somewhere else. LaPorta spoke to the media on Friday to clarify that "somewhere else" would not be his first choice.

"I feel bad if there was any sort of distraction to the team or my teammates or the coaches, but I think there was maybe a bit of a misconception with, I guess — my intentions are I want to play for this team," LaPorta said. "I give everything I have. My teammates do, as well. They all love me, respect me and support me, and they want to see me be happy and be compensated."

LaPorta has been disappointed with the offers the Lions have given him on a long-term extension, but he said he and his pregnant wife are still hoping to stay in Detroit for years.

"I guess I wouldn't expect anybody else to really even care, but emotionally for me and my family, it's an important thing for us," LaPorta said. "We want to have stability. We're excited, in the coming months, we're gonna have our first kid, me and my wife. We're gonna welcome our baby girl into the world in Metro Detroit. We want to be here with the Lions. I guess I'm getting emotional about it, but in the grand scheme of things, it's really a business. And you have to respect what the front office is doing because they're the ones calling the shots. They're the ones that brought me in. This is my first team. They've been nothing but supportive of me and my career."

LaPorta is in the fourth and final year of his rookie contract, and his base salary this year is $5.675 million. He knows he's lucky to make the money he's already making, but his contract is still a far cry from what the highest-paid tight ends in the NFL are making.

"We're very blessed. I'm getting paid millions of dollars this year," LaPorta said. "But also, when I reflect on other people in the league, I feel like I'm doing just as good a job if not better, and I want to be paid like those guys."

item.title: Seahawks sent mixed signals about whether Zach Charbonnet would play on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Seahawks sent plenty of mixed signals this week regarding the question of whether running back Zach Charbonnet would play on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
The Seahawks sent plenty of mixed signals this week regarding the question of whether running back Zach Charbonnet would play on Sunday. On Friday, the decision came.

He will not play.

Charbonnet, who suffered a torn ACL in the divisional-round win over the 49ers in January, returned to practice on October 1. He was moved to the active roster this week, and he fully participated in practice on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday.

“Zach is going to have a full week’s worth of reps, so that’s exciting," coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Monday. "There is a possibility that you can see him on Sunday in some capacity, so that is exciting.”

Speaking to reporters on Friday, Macdonald's explanation created the impression that Charbonnet not playing on Sunday was the plan all along.

"We’re going along with the plan," Macdonald said. "Plan was to get a great week’s worth of work and see where we’re at. We’re going to take it into next week. It’s part of the plan. Zach’s doing great and we’ll go into next week and see how it goes.”

The situation doesn't violate the injury-reporting rules, even if the Seahawks arguably created the impression Charbonnet would play.

Actually, the Seahawks could have milked the uncertainty for two more days. Charbonnet could have been listed as questionable on Friday, with the decision announced on Sunday that he won't be among the active players.

Still, it feels odd. Especially since Ian Rapoport of ESPNFL said on Friday's Pat McAfee Show that Rapoport expects Charbonnet to "play and play a lot" on Sunday night. (The clip apparently was deleted from Twitter, but it's still in the YouTube version of the episode.)

At a time when more and more fans are skeptical of the impact of gambling and prediction-market influences on the flow of information (and/or misinformation), this is another tangible piece of grist for the tinfoil-hat mill.

item.title: President Trump on Sunday's game in Paris: "The NFL probably could have postponed"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The NFL plans to press forward with Sunday's game between the Steelers and Saints in Paris.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL plans to press forward with Sunday's game between the Steelers and Saints in Paris.

Asked about the situation by reporters on Friday, President Trump expressed misgivings about the decision.

“Well, you worry about it," he said. "It's not — I think maybe it’s looking like tomorrow's gonna be a bad day in France. So you worry about it. I would have said the NFL could have probably postponed that match, if you want to know the truth. Because France is really in trouble."

Postponement isn't really possible, given the NFL's schedule. Relocation would make the most sense, with the game moving to one of the two NFL-ready stadiums in London. (As best we can tell, both Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and Wembley Stadium are available.)

For now, the NFL's attitude is "the show must go on." Even if the show could end up being something far different than what the NFL has envisioned.

item.title: Kenneth Walker III, who had blood clots in high school, says Jalen Hurts flying is "crazy"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III dealt with blood clots in his lungs in high school.
item.content:encoded:
Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III dealt with blood clots in his lungs in high school. He thought his football career would be over, before it even got started.

During his Friday press conference, he was asked about Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts, who is currently dealing with blood clots in his lungs.

"Yeah, honestly, just stay positive," Walker said. "You know, obviously, I guess you know about what happened in high school, like, with the blood clots and everything.  And he went on the flight, huh, and everything? Yeah, that's crazy.

"You know, honestly, just stay positive, and, you know, do all the things necessary that he need to do, like, to get his body back right. But, yeah, I'll be praying for him, because that's not something, you know, we should take lightly."

Walker's reaction to the fact that Hurts flew to London and back again isn't uncommon. And with neither the Eagles nor the league providing any real clarity on how that came to be, everyone will have to wait for the results of the investigation requested by the NFL Players Association.

If, of course, the results of that investigation are shared with the public.

item.title: Three teams could be undefeated through seven weeks, which is a rarity
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Entering Week 7, three teams are undefeated.
item.content:encoded:
Entering Week 7, three teams are undefeated. If three teams exit Week 7 undefeated, it will be a rarity.

The 49ers take their 6-0 record to Atlanta. The 5-0 Chiefs face the Seahawks in Seattle. The 5-0 Vikings play the Colts in Minneapolis.

Via NBC Sports research, only twice since the merger have three or more teams been undefeated through seven weeks of a season (with the exception of the 1982 strike year).

In 2009, three teams were unbeaten through seven weeks: the Saints, Colts, and Broncos. In 2015, five teams were perfect through seven weeks: the Panthers, Packers, Broncos, Patriots, and Bengals.

On both occasions, two of the unbeaten teams through seven weeks made it to the Super Bowl. In 2009, it was the Colts and the Saints. In 2015, the Panthers and the Broncos played in the Super Bowl.

The 49ers last went 7-0 in 2019. That year, they made it to the Super Bowl, losing to the Chiefs. The Chiefs last went 6-0 in 2024, when they made it to the Super Bowl for the third straight year, losing to the Eagles. The Vikings last went 6-0 in 2009. They lost to the Saints in the NFC Championship.

item.title: George Pickens: "I'm doing what they tell me to do"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Thursday, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer had some things to say about receiver George Pickens.
item.content:encoded:
On Thursday, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer had some things to say about receiver George Pickens. The message was that Pickens needs to do more during the plays in which he doesn't get the ball.

That's not how Pickens heard it.

“Well, I’m doing what they tell me to do," Pickens told reporters on Friday, via Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram. "So, do what they tell me to do.”

As to the specific message from Schottenheimer that Pickens needs to do a better job of blocking, Pickens didn't take it as something that was intended only for him.

“I feel like if you narrow the comments down, you’re talking about the team," Pickens said. "Most definitely, I feel like as a team, just keep improving.”

Pickens can take it however he wants. And he's right; improvement across the board is needed.

Still, it sure seemed like Schottenheimer was singling out Pickens. If Pickens doesn't want to take it that way, that's his prerogative.

Defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen), tight end Dallas Goedert (knee), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), linebacker Nolan Smith (concussion), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were out of practice again.

Guard Landon Dickerson (knee, pectoral), linebacker Jonathan Greenard (ankle), linebacker Jalyx Hunt (knee, ankle), defensive tackle Moro Ojomo (abdomen) and guard Tyler Steen (shoulder) joined Barkley as limited participants.

He has not played since Week 4 when he was injured against the 49ers. Surtain had a third consecutive limited practice on Friday after returning to practice this week.

The Broncos ruled out running back Tyler Badie (thumb), outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle). None practiced this week.

Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) improved to a full participant on Friday after being limited in Denver's first two practices of the week. Waddle was not assigned a game status.

Cornerback Riley Moss (ribs) was also a full participant on Friday and not given an injury designation.

item.title: Former Rams RB Lawrence McCutcheon dies at 76
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Former Rams running back Lawrence McCutcheon died Friday, the team announced.
item.content:encoded:
Former Rams running back Lawrence McCutcheon died Friday, the team announced. He was 76.

McCutcheon played eight seasons with the Rams (1972-79) and was a five-time Pro Bowl selection and second-team All-Pro honoree.

"It is with great sadness that we share the passing of our husband, brother, father, grandfather, and great-grandfather, Lawrence McCutcheon," the McCutcheon family said in a statement. "Clutch passed away on Oct. 23 with family at his bedside following a long, courageous battle with Parkinson's disease.

"Through a decade-long playing career and another 32 years in the Rams' front office, Clutch earned the respect and admiration of teammates, opposing players, colleagues and fans alike. Clutch will be missed and remembered forever.

"We are thankful to those in our community who have reached out with love and support. In lieu of flowers, we ask that those wishing to honor Clutch please donate to the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's research."

McCutcheon also played for Denver, Seattle and Buffalo, retiring after the 1981 season.

He finished his career with 1,521 carries for 6,578 yards and 26 touchdowns, adding 198 catches for 1,799 yards and 13 touchdowns. McCutcheon played 109 games with 82 starts.

“The Los Angeles Rams are deeply saddened by the passing of Lawrence McCutcheon," the team said in a statement. "His impact on this organization spanned generations, and he embodied what it means to be a Ram. A five-time Pro Bowl running back and once the franchise’s all-time leading rusher, he later served in our front office as a scout and director of player personnel. His legacy is woven into the fabric of our team.

"We extend our heartfelt condolences to the McCutcheon family as we celebrate a life that gave so much to the Rams and to our game.”

item.title: Vikings release RB Deejay Dallas
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Vikings released running back Deejay Dallas on Friday, according to the NFL's personnel notice.
item.content:encoded:
The Vikings released running back Deejay Dallas on Friday, according to the NFL's personnel notice.

The move makes room for running back Jordan Mason's return to the active roster. Mason fractured his thumb in the season opener against the Packers, and the Vikings placed him on injured reserve Sept. 16.

He has a questionable designation for Sunday's game, but Dallas' release signals that Mason will play.

Dallas is not subject to waivers and could sign back to the team's practice squad on Saturday and be activated for Sunday's game, if the Vikings so choose.

Dallas has played 40 offensive snaps and 92 on special teams in five games this season. He has seven touches for 44 yards.

Defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), cornerback Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), and edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (illness) are also off the injury report and are set to play.

item.title: NFL admits a penalty by the Cowboys in Week 5 was assessed against the Bucs
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The NFL has admitted a rather embarrassing officiating mistake from Week 5: When Buccaneers defensive lineman Calijah Kancey was called for illegal hands to the face, it was actually a Cowboys player who put his hands in Kancey's face, and somehow the wrong team got assessed the penalty when it was time to step off the yardage.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL has admitted a rather embarrassing officiating mistake from Week 5: When Buccaneers defensive lineman Calijah Kancey was called for illegal hands to the face, it was actually a Cowboys player who put his hands in Kancey's face, and somehow the wrong team got assessed the penalty when it was time to step off the yardage.

In the weekly officiating video, NFL officiating and rules analyst Walt Anderson said Cowboys guard Tyler Booker put his hands in Kancey's face but somehow that was miscommunicated as Kancey committing the penalty. Anderson said when the on-field officials make a mistake that blatant, the league officiating office should correct it immediately.

"Were going to have a foul called on No. 94 on the defensive team for illegal hands to the face," Anderson said. "The only action relative to any hands is really by the offensive player here. So this is the type of play that the Competition Committee has instructed officiating that if objective information in terms of just asking the officials, 'Are we sure we have the right number of the player here?' that we can end up assisting with this. Because it's clearly not a foul by No. 94. If there is illegal use of hands, it's obviously by No. 52 of the offense."

Kancey made clear in the moment that he knew it was a bad call, but there's nothing a player can do to fix a bad call against him. The New York officiating office could have fixed it, but didn't.

item.title: Injuries could increase Aaron Donald's playing time
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Aaron Donald may be privately thinking, "I'm too old for this shit."
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Donald may be privately thinking, "I'm too old for this shit."

Regardless, the rash of injuries along the Rams' defensive line could result in the 35-year-old defensive tackle, who returned last month from a two-year retirement, taking more reps than he has.

“I'm going to just be out there playing," Donald told reporters on Friday. "However that rotation is going to be, it's going to be. We never have to set a snap — we just go as the game goes and have what that is. If it's 30 plays, 40 plays, 50 plays, 60 plays, that's what it's going to be.”

This week, the Rams placed both nose tackle Poona Ford and defensive end Kobie Turner on injured reserve. Linebacker Myles Garrett has been on IR since the days following Week 1.

Also on Thursday, defensive coordinator Chris Shula was asked whether the injuries would result in more reps for Donald.

“That's hard to say," Shula said. "I think it definitely depends on the flow of the game and a lot of things like that. A lot of things go into it. We have a general snap count that he's always going to have going into the game. I don't think we would go crazily past that, but it's going to be hard if it's a tight game and he's at that number. Just like one of those pitchers in the ninth inning, you're probably going to leave him in for a few extra snaps.”

In four games this season, Donald has played 33 snaps in Week 2 (56.9 percent), 35 snaps in Week 3 (52.2 percent), 43 snaps in Week 5 (67.2 percent), and 42 snaps in Week 6 (58.3 percent).

Donald, whose interest in returning was sparked by the trade for Garrett, has yet to play in a game with the 2025 NFL Defensive Player of the Year. On Sunday against the 3-3 Raiders, the Rams may need Donald to turn back the clock to his pre-retirement form — and workload — in order to avoid falling to 2-5 through seven games.

item.content:encoded:
Veteran cornerback Trevon Diggs won't be on the Seahawks' active roster for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.

Diggs was released on Friday. The move opens a roster spot that the Seahawks could use to activate guard Anthony Bradford from injured reserve. Bradford has been designated for return and has no injury designation for this week.

item.title: Ben Johnson on Cole Kmet: He's going to be sorely missed
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Bears coach Ben Johnson confirmed that tight end Cole Kmet will miss the rest of the season on injured reserve after a right knee injury Thursday night.
item.content:encoded:
Bears coach Ben Johnson confirmed that tight end Cole Kmet will miss the rest of the season on injured reserve after a right knee injury Thursday night.

The Bears made the move official Friday.

In seven games, Kmet made 10 catches for 87 yards and a touchdown.

Johnson said the Bears will miss Kmet, who has missed only one game in seven seasons.

"He’s one of my favorites for a number of reasons," Johnson said, via Adam Jahns of CHGO_Sports. "I still remember him at the combine coming out and how much I loved him in that slight interaction we had there. To be able to be in the same room with him for the last year and a half, I've got so much respect for the player that he is, but also the person, the leader. He's everything we want to be about here. He's one of the glue guys. He's one of the guys that I can count on, whether it's a messaging standpoint or getting the pulse of the team. He's going to be sorely missed. Really, he's Chicago. He's been here his whole life, and he's a big part of our heartbeat. So, it stinks. It does. I hate it for him. I hate it for his teammates as well. And yet the train keeps rolling along. Someone else has to step up. Fortunately, we talked about this last week: Just our practice squad, the way we've been developing, the way they've been working, I think we've got some good options here on this roster. So, yeah, we're going to miss him."

item.title: A.J. Brown: I've got to put my best foot forward, try to make plays and keep going
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Patriots wide receiver A.J.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown expects more of himself, but he is trying to be patient and not frustrated.

The Patriots played two games in four days in Brown's return from a right high ankle sprain, and he made only six catches on 16 targets for 75 yards. He dropped four passes, including three in Sunday's win over the Jets.

“I’m a vet. I understand how the game goes,” Brown said, via Eric Edholm of yahoo!sports. “It’s just how the game is. I know what type of player I am, and I know that that’s always the case, every time I line up I get a lot of attention. Teams try to take me away and it gives a lot of opportunities to other guys to make plays and soften that up for me. And then whenever I get my shots, I have to make them.”

The Patriots traded a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder for Brown, who requested the trade from the Eagles. He was frustrated with the offense and quarterback Jalen Hurts in Philadelphia last season.

Now, he's with Drake Maye and is trying to find his way back to being a No. 1 wide receiver.

He was asked after Thursday night's loss to the Bears whether he needed an adjustment period with a new team.

"I guess you could say that," Brown said. "But there's no time for that. . . . I just gotta try to put my best foot forward and try to make plays and keep going."

item.title: Lamar Jackson officially questionable for Ravens-Bengals
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Jackson told reporters on Friday he's heading in the right direction to play on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
After a week of limited practices, Baltimore quarterback Lamar Jackson is officially questionable for Sunday’s game against Cincinnati.

The Ravens made the designation official with their final injury report of the week on Friday afternoon.

Jackson has been sidelined for the last two games by a sprained ankle. Though it’s been reported that Jackson did not have a high-ankle sprain, he said after practice that is, in fact, what he’s been dealing with.

“Ian Rapoport said that? [Is] he part of the training staff?" Jackson said, eliciting laughter, via transcript from the team. ”We can’t go off Ian Rapoport. He [is] just reporting. Somebody probably told him that too though, so [I] can’t blame him.

“But my staff told me it was a high ankle sprain, so we [are] going with what [head certified athletic trainer] Adrian [Dixon] told me. I’m going with what Adrian told me.”

Jackson also noted that he’s “heading in the right direction.”

“I can’t call it right now,” Jackson said. “I still [have] got a grace period, so we’ll see, but hopefully. I feel like I”m heading in the right direction right now.

“I don’t have a number, but I don’t feel like I have to be 100,” Jackson added. “If I can just be out there and tolerate the pain in my ankle, [then] that’s it. If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play. But [if] I’m restricted and I can't do what I do, [then] I’m not helping [anybody]. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and be hit, that’s not helping my team at all. That’s just me. I feel like I’m being selfish, because it’s about me at that point, for me to go out there and be hurt.”

Tyler Huntley would start if Jackson is not available.

Elsewhere on the injury report, safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) and outside linebacker Tavius Robinson (pectoral) are out. Robinson’s pectoral injury will keep him out for the rest of the season.

Cornerback T.J. Tampa (knee) is doubtful after he was limited all week while in his 21-day practice window. Defensive tackle Broderick Washington (ankle) is questionable.

Tight end Mark Andrews (hand), receiver Rashod Bateman (shoulder), outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson (finger), tight end Matthew Hibner (hand), offensive lineman Vega Ioane (ankle), center Cam Jurgens (concussion), guard John Simpson (groin), offensive tackle Ronnie Stanley (toe/ankle), and guard Andrew Vorhees (foot) are all off the injury report and set to play.

item.title: Cam Skattebo is expected to return to the running back mix on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Giants running back Cam Skattebo, after having a key overtime fumble in Week 5, played only six snaps and had no touches in Week 6.
item.content:encoded:
Giants running back Cam Skattebo, after having a key overtime fumble in Week 5, played only six snaps and had no touches in Week 6. He apparently has been released from coach John Harbaugh's doghouse.

Via Jordan Raanan of ESPN, Harbaugh said Friday that Skattebo had a "good week" of practice, and that he should return to the running back rotation on Sunday at Houston.

"It's been good, you know; I think I got taught a lesson," Skattebo said, via Raanan. "I don't know if that's from them or from myself, but I kind of had to step back and look at it and figure out why I was doing the things I was doing, what was happening. Came to practice, corrected those things, worked on them. Ready to go back out there and play ball. . . .

"I took care of the ball during practice, and whatever my role is on Sunday is going to be my role and I'm going to give it everything I've got."

Beyond Skattebo being frozen out of the game plan against the Saints, he and the rest of the team got a wakeup call regarding who's in charge when running back Najee Harris was cut only two days after publicly questioning the approach to the run game.

"Nobody's safe," Skattebo said. "It's as simple as that. I think when we go on the field and we perform, if we're not performing, we understand there's a possibility of not being here. If I don't perform, I know there's a possibility of me not being here. We came in this week. We continue to work. We know where we're at. We know what we have. If we put that to display, we're going to be just fine."

For the season, Skattebo has 81 carries for 294 yards and one touchdown. He's averaging 3.6 yards per carry.

Last week, three Giants running backs had carries in the 34-27 loss to New Orleans. Tyrone Tracy ran six times for 18 yards, Devin Singletary received four attempts for 14 yards, and Harris had two rushes for four yards. Quarterback J.J. McCarthy led the team in rushing with 26 yards on two attempts.

With McCarthy getting his first start less than four weeks arriving via trade, the Giants need to have a solid effort on the ground to make it easier for McCarthy to operate the passing game. Skattebo will get a chance to provide the punch the Giants were missing in Week 6.

The Browns took a number of players off their injury report on Friday, but they also made one significant addition.

Cornerback Denzel Ward was limited in the team's final practice before facing the Titans because of a hand injury. Ward is listed as questionable to play on Sunday.

Head coach Todd Monken told reporters that he is hopeful that Ward will be able to play. If he does, he'll join offensive tackle Tytus Howard, defensive tackle Maliek Collins, defensive tackle Mason Graham, center Elgron Jenkins, running back Quinshon Judkins, and linebacker Carson Schwesinger as none of them have injury designations.

Safety Grant Delpit (concussion, shoulder), running back Dylan Sampson (knee), and linebacker Quincy Williams (neck) are also listed as questionable. Defensive tackle Kalia Davis (quad), quarterback Dillon Gabriel (back), defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. (ankle), and offensive lineman Teven Jenkins (back) have all been ruled out.
